newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds rally, depos sink, ecu/drs up.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds rally, depos sink, ecu/drs up.

text.p: Greek depos dropped 100 to 150 basis points across-the-board, forex forwards were down and bonds rallied after the central bank effectively cut its overnight rate by 200 basis points, dealers said.
Ecu was gathering strength against the drachma, breaking through the 307 level in late trade in a nervous market.

"Depos plummeted 100 to 150 basis points after the central bank's announcement and short-term rates fell more than long-term rates," a money dealer said. "The move surprised the market that is trying to adjust to the changes."

Bank of Greece announced changes in the conduct of monetary policy today aiming to increase the effectiveness of its market interventions and prepare for the expected operating framework to be used under EMU.
The central bank will institute regular weekly repo and depo volume or interest rate tenders to influence short-term rates, it said.
"With these tenders, the bank will drain or offer liquidity at interest rates fluctuating between the maximum rate (Lombard) and the minimum rate set by the new framework of accepting deposits."

The central bank will also accept interbank depos up to 300 billion drachmas from the market at 11.90 percent and amounts exceeding 300 billion at 9.90 percent effective March 28, it said in a statement.

Bank of Greece will set a depo ceiling for each credit institution which will be a function of its market share in the domestic market defined by its loans, placements in Greek government securities, drachma interbank market and reserves deposited with the central bank.
The depo ceiling will apply to the first base deposit rate of 11.90 percent, it added.
There will be no depo limit per credit institution for sums exceeding the ceiling at the second rate of 9.90 percent, it said.

"We have to wait-and-see what amounts the central bank will drain through its weekly repo and depo tenders before deciding where interest rates are going to settle," said a senior dealer. "It would have been better if there were no such abrupt change in rates."
The new element in the central bank's announcement was the effective 200 basis point cut in its overnight intervention to 9.90 percent that has fuelled a bond rally, he said.
Bond dealers said prices of FRNs and fixed coupon bonds skyrocketed after the central bank's announcement due to the substantially reduced funding cost for banks.
"The funding cost has been cut substantially and bonds rallied subsequently," a foreign bank dealer said. "Fixed bonds benefited more than FRNs from the central bank's move."
Dealers said bond prices had risen by 1.0 to 0.60 percent on the news.
The mark was quoted at 157.55/75 from Monday's 157.565 fix, the dollar at 265.97/07 drachmas from 266.400 and the Ecu at 305.97/07 from 305.640 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma is trading around 307.20/40 in late trade after opening at 305.90/10," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The major questions are whether the central bank will stick to its announced forex policy for 1997 and whether foreign investors will be willing to take Greek risk at these rate differentials."

The central bank checked $/drachma prices three or four times today and sold a small amount of ecus for drachmas at the fixing showing some concern over the strength of the ecu, another forex dealer said.
Ecu/drachma was set at 306.52 at the central bank's fixing.
